claims.proposition: Hunk selections choose deletion/insertion operations, with mixed outcomes; show synthesized result and unambiguous pane meaning.

evidence.exact_quote:
- [diff.lua](https://github.com/julienvincent/hunk.nvim/blob/c8a8e7b6973576f63e5bf39aa8338d7f37f4dc53/lua/hunk/api/diff.lua#L92-L106), [S00017](research-evidence/sources/S00017/text.txt):100–105, retains an old line when its left-side deletion is **not** selected, and emits a new line when its right-side insertion **is** selected. For one replaced line, selecting neither keeps old; selecting both produces new; selecting only right retains old and adds new; selecting only left removes old without inserting new. This is a source-derived example, not a runtime observation.
- [init.lua](https://github.com/julienvincent/hunk.nvim/blob/c8a8e7b6973576f63e5bf39aa8338d7f37f4dc53/lua/hunk/init.lua#L62-L109), [S00016](research-evidence/sources/S00016/text.txt):62–88, pairs by offset within a hunk, rather than semantic code identity. Lines 90–109 toggle an entire hunk on both sides. File selection covers both sides (18–29).
- [output tests](research-evidence/sources/S00015/text.txt):83–117 and [diff tests](research-evidence/sources/S00067/text.txt):18–40 explicitly assert mixed old/new partial results. They support the deletion/insertion interpretation behind the confusion reported in #30.

**Lesson retained:** show synthesized resulting content and make the meaning of a selected deletion/insertion visible. Pairing is helpful but does not remove the need to explain partial results or unequal hunk sizes.

The baseline diff selector has read-only left/right buffers and applies selected deletions/insertions only on final acceptance. A result preview could show the actual synthesized content, including both-lines/neither-line outcomes, before committing a selection. Keep three alternatives distinct: read-only synthesized preview, editable center pane, or select-then-edit staged review.

- [Issue #6 pane-label discussion](https://github.com/julienvincent/hunk.nvim/issues/6#issuecomment-4397260720), S00033: identify result and revision context; ours/theirs can reverse. The acquired jj external-merge implementation passes base/left/right/output/path/marker_length, not revision-label variables (S00041 lines 222–262). This does not establish that integrations can never supply extra metadata.

Unresolved: behavior of undo after manual edits, unequal hunks, ambiguous application order, remaining-conflict detection, baseline-branch integration, exact bytes on output, and whether result editing should be allowed during split selection as well as conflict resolution. The experimental commit's message says PoC and contains “Closes #6”; the issue remains open and the assigned baseline revision contains no merge module. Do not promote the branch into baseline capability.

evidence.exact_quote:
The [accept/quit implementation](https://github.com/julienvincent/hunk.nvim/blob/c8a8e7b6973576f63e5bf39aa8338d7f37f4dc53/lua/hunk/init.lua#L123-L141), S00016:123–141, calls `write_changeset` and then `qa` for accept. Quit calls `cq` without calling the writer; optional quit confirmation is configurable. Buffers are read-only/nonmodifiable in the normal diff UI (S00038:25–34). The intended selection-cancel path is supported.

The README phrase “no changes will be written” needs a boundary. In independent native jj [external.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/c5ba4ea0b011fbc8d532d74b6cf8493911618cf5/cli/src/merge_tools/external.rs#L384-L443), [S00041](research-evidence/sources/S00041/text.txt):411–443, failed spawn or unsuccessful editor exit returns before output snapshotting. [Diffedit test source](research-evidence/sources/S00065/text.txt):107–122 and 786–802 makes a temporary deletion then fails and asserts the repository diff remains unchanged. This supports rejection of editor output, not rollback of every earlier effect.

Native split calls `workspace_helper` before selecting the diff and only finishes its split transaction afterward ([S00044](research-evidence/sources/S00044/text.txt):280–294, 421–422); squash has the same ordering ([S00058](research-evidence/sources/S00058/text.txt):192, 269, 338–350, 456). [Workspace handling](research-evidence/sources/S00043/text.txt):459–516 snapshots when allowed, and 2128–2235 can commit a separate “snapshot working copy” operation. Thus cancellation can reject the split/squash edit while leaving a prior snapshot. A crash or nonzero editor exit is not proof of unchanged repository state or unchanged generic input directories.

evidence.exact_quote: **Do not conflate merge cancellation with diff cancellation.** Native external merge invocation is per file and explicitly leaves directory mode as a TODO (S00041:337–381). On failure after earlier files, it returns a partially resolved tree. [resolve.rs](research-evidence/sources/S00062/text.txt):114–146 commits that tree before returning the partial-resolution error. This directly supports preserving saved/pending/failed file states in a future multi-file conflict workflow.

Primary jj code at `c5ba4ea0b011fbc8d532d74b6cf8493911618cf5` supports the limitation: [external.rs lines 337–381](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/c5ba4ea0b011fbc8d532d74b6cf8493911618cf5/cli/src/merge_tools/external.rs#L337-L381), S00041, invokes the merge tool once per file and explicitly leaves directory invocation as a TODO. Failure on a later file returns the already-resolved tree plus a partial-resolution error. [resolve.rs lines 114–146](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/c5ba4ea0b011fbc8d532d74b6cf8493911618cf5/cli/src/commands/resolve.rs#L114-L146), S00062, commits that tree before returning the error.

Consequently, the diff-editor nonzero-exit contract cannot be generalized to “cancel a multi-file resolve and nothing was saved.” This is a source-backed distinction, not a demonstrated runtime in this workspace.

Unresolved: separate app-level conflict session versus future native directory invocation; explicit saved/pending/failed file states; resume after partial completion; trustworthy pane identity and result labels. Keep the experimental `MergeEditor` and baseline `DiffEditor` as different protocols until integration is verified.

claims.proposition: Partial hunk output normalizes a missing final newline, while whole-file moves use a different path; preserve bytes, EOF and metadata explicitly.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Missing final newline:** `read_file_as_lines` removes the final empty split element (57–62); `write_file` appends `"\n"` to every emitted line (79–91). Partial selections call that pipeline (S00007:91–96), without retaining an EOF flag. A nonempty partial result lacking a final newline is therefore normalized. Whole-file branches move left/right files (71–99), so this is not the path taken by every acceptance, including a selection that becomes “all selected.”

At the assigned revision, partial selection reconstructs a file as lines and appends LF to each emitted line. This loses missing-final-newline information; whole-file selection uses `mv` and should not be described as taking the same rewrite path. The API also mutates the supplied left/right trees by moving files, so “separate output” is not a promise to preserve its inputs.

Follow-up evidence matrix: two- and three-directory operation; one versus all selected hunks; missing final newline and CRLF; empty/new/deleted files; executable-only and content-plus-mode changes; file↔symlink and dangling links; inaccessible input/output; failed/partial writes and command errors; inputs after successful accept. Record bytes, type, mode and errors separately. Do not claim that every permission/symlink case is broken; it is not established by these sources.

Alternative to evaluate: preserve bytes/EOF and metadata explicitly, use checked non-destructive copies or staged writes, propagate every filesystem failure to nonzero editor exit, and review the synthesized result before acceptance. No upstream code was run.

claims.proposition: A shared registry lock and action token protect participating spawn/cancel calls; exited leaders, pipes, close and cancel have distinct completion semantics.

evidence.exact_quote:
1. **Identity and scope:** a PID-keyed registry stores the `Child`, optional `SyncToken` and `signaled` flag (33–48). Token identity uses pointer identity for the shared atomic flag (98–100). `CURRENT_SYNC` is thread-local; `enter` temporarily replaces it and restores prior scope on drop (29–31, 89–111).
2. **Spawn/cancel race protection:** output obtains that scope, configures the child, and checks `closed`/canceled while holding the same mutex used to spawn/register (122–154). Cancel first latches intent and then sweeps matching entries under the mutex (59–79). A spawn that wins the lock is registered before the sweep; a later spawn sees canceled. This protects participating registry calls, not arbitrary subprocess APIs.
3. **Exited leaders and pipes:** cancel marks `signaled` only if `try_wait()` reports a still-running leader, but signals its group even after leader exit (70–75). The output entry stays registered while pipes are read, which supports freeing descendant-held pipes in the intended Unix case.
4. **Completion and classification:** stdout is read while another thread reads stderr (233–251); output then reaps/polls the registered leader (155–157, 168–189). `CoreError::Canceled` requires `signaled && !status.success()` (158–160). A late cancel can free pipes while preserving a successful leader result. Pipe/reap errors instead become `Internal`; the cancellation flag is not a substitute for observed process status. Normal successful pipe completion is not proof that every possible descendant exited.
5. **Close is different:** close seals the registry and signals all entries (192–201), then waits the grace and sends forceful termination to entries still present (204–220). It does not set their `signaled` cancellation flag or itself join/reap every worker. The test expects a killed-on-close child to return an unsuccessful `Output`, not `Canceled`.
6. **Timing:** the 200 ms constant and field note that a fetch survived SIGTERM are present at 25–27. Escalation runs in a background thread for cancel, synchronously through the grace for close. This is an escalation policy, not a guaranteed 200 ms total lifetime or an independently confirmed incident receipt.

claims.proposition: Unix process-group signaling and Windows taskkill are different, ignore termination results, and do not establish a 200 ms completion deadline; Job Objects are an unimplemented alternative.

evidence.exact_quote:
| [Unix source](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/command_process/unix.rs), [S00010](research-evidence/sources/S00010/text.txt):4–16 | `process_group(0)` and `kill(-pid, SIGTERM/SIGKILL)`. Kill results are ignored. [POSIX](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/kill.html), [S00053](research-evidence/sources/S00053/text.txt):19–29, confirms negative PID targets permitted members of that process group, not all descendants regardless of group membership. |
| [Windows source](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/command_process/windows.rs), [S00011](research-evidence/sources/S00011/text.txt):3–15 | Group configuration is a no-op. Termination synchronously invokes `taskkill /PID <pid> /T`, with `/F` for force, suppressing output and ignoring execution/status results. [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/taskkill), [S00056](research-evidence/sources/S00056/text.txt):44–51, defines tree and force options. This is not SIGTERM/SIGKILL, and neither source proves the exited-leader case on Windows. Because `.status()` runs under the registry lock, cancel latency includes that external command, not merely latching a flag. |
| [Process tests](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/command_process/tests.rs), [S00012](research-evidence/sources/S00012/text.txt) | Six tests cover stubborn group termination on close (8–32), closed-registry refusal (34–41), token isolation (43–72), canceled-action refusal of later children (74–91), cancellation after stderr output (93–124), and successful exited leader with descendant-held pipes (126–153). The last explicitly expects success. The module is `cfg(all(test, unix))` (S00003:6–7). These are unexecuted intended assertions, not Windows evidence or an exhaustive race/timeout proof. |

**Alternative retained:** [Windows Job Objects](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects), [S00055](research-evidence/sources/S00055/text.txt):35–45, 67–74, provide process association, inherited child membership, termination and kill-on-close, with breakaway/nesting caveats. They deserve investigation as stronger managed containment; the inspected JayJay implementation does not use them. Unix descendants leaving the group, signal failures, open pipes after leader exit, and deterministic shutdown joining remain runtime questions.

At `3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea`, [Unix implementation](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/command_process/unix.rs), S00010, creates a group and signals `-pid`; [Windows implementation](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/command_process/windows.rs), S00011, does no group setup and synchronously runs `taskkill /PID … /T`, later `/F`. Both discard termination results. A 200 ms grace is not an end-to-end deadline.

[POSIX kill](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/kill.html), S00053 lines 19–29, targets eligible processes sharing the process-group ID; it is not arbitrary descendant enumeration. [Microsoft taskkill](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/taskkill), S00056 lines 44–51, defines `/T` and `/F`, but does not establish this implementation's behavior after the leader disappears. The Unix-only tests S00012 cover exited-leader/held-pipe cleanup and stubborn groups; none were executed here.

Alternative: [Windows Job Objects](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects), S00055 lines 35–45 and 67–74, support association, inherited child membership, group termination and kill-on-close. Evaluate association/spawn races, breakaway rules, nested jobs and assignment failures before adoption. This alternative is not implemented by the inspected JayJay module.

Unresolved matrix: cancel racing spawn and natural exit; leader already exited; descendants retaining both pipes; descendants leaving the group; ignored termination and permission errors; blocked pipe reads; close versus cancel result classification; deterministic worker/reap completion and Windows latency. Collect actual process/pipe/exit receipts rather than interpreting the cancellation request or UI click as completion.

claims.proposition: Thread-local cancellation scopes and exact environment coverage have gaps: generic helpers and login-shell PATH probing use other spawn paths.

evidence.exact_quote:
[command.rs](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/command.rs), [S00031](research-evidence/sources/S00031/text.txt):15–20, resolves jj, sets the repository cwd and uses the registry. But generic `command_output_in` uses ordinary `.output()` outside it (50–63). Quiet jj calls discard the whole result (37–39); ordinary non-success output becomes `Internal` with combined output text (66–100). Thus error distinctions exist, but exit codes, transport categories and stdout/stderr are not all preserved as structured caller errors. A `Canceled` error itself contains no process-output receipt in this path.

The assigned [sync caller](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/git/sync.rs), [S00030](research-evidence/sources/S00030/text.txt):9–26 and 67–83, enters a token scope for normal push/pull. This supports binding synchronous registry-routed jj calls within those entry points. A separate multi-bookmark helper does not enter a token itself (31–47); it could inherit an enclosing scope. Neither thread-local storage nor the comment “every jj process” proves automatic propagation to new threads or all generic subprocesses.

[environment.rs](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/environment.rs), [S00034](research-evidence/sources/S00034/text.txt):48–89, 128–183, resolves tools using inherited/login-shell/fallback paths and adjusts PATH and SSH_AUTH_SOCK. It does not freeze or record an exact full environment. Its login-shell PATH probe spawns outside the registry (258–282), polls a leader deadline, and then uses `wait_with_output` after successful leader exit; descendant-held stdout is an unresolved separate boundary. These are concrete limits to a universal “all subprocesses are canceled” claim, not observed leaks.

[command_process.rs](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/command_process.rs), S00003, binds a token through thread-local `CURRENT_SYNC` and restores previous scope on drop. This covers registry-routed jj calls within the synchronous entered action, not arbitrary commands or newly spawned threads automatically. The reviewed push/pull entry points enter that scope (S00030 lines 10 and 73).

[command.rs](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/command.rs), S00031 lines 15–20, sets repository cwd and routes jj through the registry; lines 50–63 route generic commands directly through `.output()` outside it. The separate multi-bookmark push helper in S00030 lines 31–47 does not create a token scope itself; callers may still supply an enclosing scope.

[environment.rs](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/environment.rs), S00034 lines 48–89 and 128–183, resolves binaries and augments PATH/SSH_AUTH_SOCK. It does not freeze or record a complete effective environment. The login-shell PATH probe (lines 258–282) spawns outside the registry. It polls the leader with a nominal two-second deadline, but on successful leader exit calls `wait_with_output`; descendant-held stdout remains a question. No such hang was observed here.

Alternative to investigate: explicit operation context passed into every relevant command runner, explicit propagation across thread boundaries, uniform registration where required, and non-secret receipts for resolved executable/version/cwd/config inputs. Keep this as a scoped completeness audit, not a claim that every helper presently leaks processes or that Windows behavior matches Unix.

claims.proposition: Cancellation intent, process result, action completion and actual local/remote effects differ; multi-step sync can publish before a canceled result, so reconcile before retry.

evidence.exact_quote:
- Push optionally tracks the bookmark first, then pushes, reloads, and finally checks cancellation (S00030:9–22). A final `Canceled` result can occur after a successful remote phase.
- Pull reads tracked names, fetches, optionally tracks, rebases to `trunk()`, reloads, checks cancellation, and performs cleanup (67–105, 116–167). Several errors are deliberately ignored. Cleanup checks cancellation before best-effort `abandon`, then records the bookmark in its result (151–155); that report alone is not a verified successful abandonment receipt.
- The [Mac UI](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/shell/mac/Sources/JayJay/Repo/ViewModel/Actions/RepoViewModel+GitActions.swift#L109-L118), [S00048](research-evidence/sources/S00048/text.txt):109–118, explicitly refreshes after cancellation because “The remote phase may have landed before the cancel took effect.” Cancel methods only call the token (46–52). [Async support](research-evidence/sources/S00057/text.txt):94–115 and 119–151 clears busy state and delivers success/failure after the operation returns. There is no automatic replay in these inspected cancel/result paths. Local refresh alone does not establish authoritative remote state.

Independent native jj source reinforces why kill/reap cannot establish rollback:

- [Git fetch implementation](research-evidence/sources/S00046/text.txt):3284–3288 states it updates Git remote-tracking branches before subsequent jj import. [CLI fetch](research-evidence/sources/S00037/text.txt):242–261 separates remote fetch, import, and transaction finish. Interruption between phases need not imply no local Git effect.
- [CLI push](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/c5ba4ea0b011fbc8d532d74b6cf8493911618cf5/cli/src/commands/git/push.rs#L598-L656), [S00045](research-evidence/sources/S00045/text.txt):598–656, calls remote push before local transaction completion; on some exported refs it can commit then return “Failed to push some bookmarks.” [Library code](research-evidence/sources/S00046/text.txt):3490–3540 updates local exported/remote-ref records after the push. A local failure or killed observer does not undo remote changes.
- “No auto-retry” is a useful recovery policy and is supported for the inspected UI cancellation path, not as a universal transport claim. The independent native fetch contains a retry loop that drops missing refspecs (S00046:3313–3342). This is different from retrying an entire user action after an uncertain cancellation.

**Lesson retained:** distinguish cancellation requested, process result, action completion, and observed local/remote effects. Preserve success when the process actually finished successfully; do not turn a cancel click into a rollback claim. Before any recovery/retry decision, identify the exact executable/version, arguments, cwd and effective configuration, then reconcile operation heads, relevant Git refs and remote state. No runtime before/after receipts were acquired in this read-only source review, and the inspected native jj version is not asserted to be JayJay's installed version.

[JayJay sync callers](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/git/sync.rs), S00030, perform bookmark tracking before push (lines 9–22), then fetch/track/rebase/reload and optional abandonment for pull (lines 67–104, 137–162). Each subprocess can complete before a later cancellation check. Quiet helpers discard errors (S00031 lines 37–39); abandonment reporting records a bookmark after a best-effort call, so UI text is not a verified per-step receipt.

[Mac cancellation presentation](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/shell/mac/Sources/JayJay/Repo/ViewModel/Actions/RepoViewModel+GitActions.swift#L109-L118), S00048, explicitly refreshes because “The remote phase may have landed before the cancel took effect.” It does not retry the canceled action in this path. S00057 lines 94–115 clears busy state in actual result callbacks, not on cancel.

Independent native evidence at jj `c5ba4ea0b011fbc8d532d74b6cf8493911618cf5` (manifest version 0.45.1, not a captured JayJay CLI version): S00046 lines 3284–3288 says fetch changes Git remote-tracking refs before jj import; S00037 lines 242–261 separates fetch/import/transaction completion. S00045 lines 598–656 pushes before finishing the local transaction and can commit partial exports then return an error. Kill/reap cannot reverse those boundaries.

Unresolved: pin executable/version/cwd/config/transport and capture pre/post jj operation heads, relevant Git refs and authoritative remote refs for controlled cancellations. Distinguish requested, observed process result, local effects and remote effects. Re-read state before deciding whether any retry is appropriate; ordinary local refresh is not proof of remote state. Also keep transport-level retries distinct: native jj fetch has a missing-refspec retry loop (S00046 lines 3313–3342), so “no retries anywhere” is unsupported.
